clue.text: Jerk cycling in hail on the move

indicators.note: in places the twitch inside the greeting word, which wraps around it
cycling sends a letter round from one end of the word to the other, like a wheel turning

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary jerk of a muscle
ave is the Latin greeting, a hail

explanation.surface: Someone twitches while riding a bike through a hailstorm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycling' suggests a bicycle, but it means moving a letter from the end of a word round to the start. Ave is the Latin greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something active is busy and moving about rather than still or dormant.

clue.text: A new chief is source of much chaos

parts.note: taken as written
N is the standard abbreviation for new
arch- as in archbishop means chief
taken as written

indicators.note: a source is where something starts, so only the start of the following word is wanted

parts.note: the opening letter of much

explanation.surface: A newly appointed boss turns out to be behind most of the disorder at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Source of much chaos' reads as one phrase about the boss, but 'source of' only picks out a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchism, the doctrine of abolishing the state, is equated by opponents with lawless disorder.

clue.text: Clobber from traveller's case with little weight

indicators.note: a case is the outside shell of something, so only the outermost letters of the preceding word count

parts.note: the first and last letters of traveller
an ounce is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: Someone is whacked with a suitcase that barely weighs anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clobber' is also British slang for clothes or gear, which fits the luggage picture, but here it is the verb meaning to beat.
explanation.definitionFit: To clobber an opponent is to beat them heavily, the same as a decisive defeat.

clue.text: Chamber's opening left covered in grain

parts.note: a vent is an opening or outlet

indicators.note: something covered in a substance is wrapped by it, so the grain word goes around the letter

parts.note: rice is a cereal grain
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A storage room's doorway sits under a layer of spilt grain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chamber' suggests a room, but the answer is an anatomical chamber.
explanation.definitionFit: A ventricle is one of the pumping cavities of the heart, or a cavity in the brain.

clue.text: Quickly get larger drink

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to grow faster and faster, like a rolling ball of packed snow
second meaning: a cocktail of advocaat and lemonade

explanation.surface: Advice to bulk up fast by downing a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb describes accelerating growth, and the noun is a Christmassy mixed drink made with egg liqueur.

clue.text: Soft cocoon in hall gets spun

definitions.note: an adjective in the sense of a soft drink

indicators.note: spun suggests whirling round, throwing the letters of the two words out of order

parts.note: the letters of these three words are the fodder

explanation.surface: A delicate silk cocoon is whirled around in a hallway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soft' looks like a description of the cocoon, but it is the definition, as in soft drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft drinks are those containing no alcohol, so soft here means free of liquor.

clue.text: Little card bearing hearts

indicators.note: a person bearing something holds it, so the card word carries the letter within it

parts.note: a card is a joker or wag, a witty person
H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games

explanation.surface: A small playing card shows the heart suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Card' and 'hearts' paint a deck of cards, but card means a comic person here.
explanation.definitionFit: A whit is a tiny amount, used as in 'not a whit', meaning not the least bit.

clue.text: Man grabs giant, totally unbridled, horse

indicators.note: unbridled means without the harness around the head, and totally applies this stripping of the outer letters to every word before it

parts.note: Man with its first and last letters removed
grabs with its first and last letters removed
giant with its first and last letters removed

explanation.surface: A man seizes a huge horse that has thrown off its bridle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man grabs giant' reads like a container instruction, but nothing goes inside anything: each of the three words simply loses its ends.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arabian is a famous breed of riding horse from the Arabian Peninsula.

clue.text: Subject characters in college ill-advisedly took up

definitions.note: a noun: one owing loyalty to a lord

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken up means read from the bottom to the top, so backwards
characters in means some of the letters printed in the following words, read straight from the text

parts.note: the run of letters straddling the two words
surface padding: completes the phrase ill-advisedly for the story

explanation.surface: A student at college unwisely took up something and regretted it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ill-advisedly' looks like an anagram signal, but the letters are hidden in 'college ill' and read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: In feudal usage a liege could be a vassal owing allegiance, that is, a subject of a lord.

clue.text: Close to a facility for sport, but not golf

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: but not means excluding, so the named letter is taken away

parts.note: a sports ground, such as a football or cricket ground
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone lives near a sports venue, though not a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: Around, meaning approximately or nearby, works as 'close to' in phrases like 'around fifty'.

clue.text: Space with endorsement, say, having turned picture

parts.note: an en is a printer's space, half an em
a visa is an endorsement stamped in a passport

indicators.note: having turned means the abbreviation for say faces the other way round

parts.note: e.g. means for example, that is, say

explanation.surface: An application for permission to enter space is approved and then reversed.
explanation.walkthrough: EN is a printing term for a space; EG is reversed to GE at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To envisage something is to form a mental image of it, to picture it in the mind.

clue.text: Out of date, we're told, scrap creamy food

parts.note: from means out of, as in 'taken from a box'
a date or period of time is an age

indicators.note: we're told means heard by ear, so the word for scrap is only matched in pronunciation

parts.note: a fray is a fight, a scrap

explanation.surface: An expired product is mentioned and then thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of date' reads as one phrase meaning stale, but it splits in two. The French word at the end is pronounced like a word for a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Fromage frais is a soft fresh French cheese with a creamy texture, eaten like yoghurt.

clue.text: Prisoner shot holding air rifle regularly in defiant manner

parts.note: a con is a convict

indicators.note: holding means the shot word grips the selected letters inside it

parts.note: to have a shot is to have a try

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the weapon's name is kept

parts.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: An inmate is shot while clutching an air rifle he regularly fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prisoner shot' suggests violence, but shot means an attempt. An aril is a seed covering, but here the letters just come from the weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting contrarily is behaving perversely, deliberately doing the opposite of what is wanted.

clue.text: Small child is matter for discussion, back to the fore

indicators.note: the back letter of the word is brought round to the front

parts.note: an item on an agenda is a matter for discussion

explanation.surface: A little child has become the topic everyone is talking about.
explanation.walkthrough: The last M of ITEM moves to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Mite is an affectionate word for a tiny child, as in 'poor little mite'.

clue.text: Anger when stuck in pad that's shared with another

indicators.note: stuck in says the answer is what was inserted, so taking the host away from the result leaves it

parts.note: something shared with another is paired
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone seethes at being stuck in a flat they share with a housemate.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: the answer is what you put into the three letters of 'pad' to make a word meaning shared with another. 'Pad' is not a flat at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Ire is a literary word for wrath or fury.

clue.text: Group of politicians bizarrely seen as rational

definitions.note: an adjective, in the sense of common-sense used before a noun

parts.note: the Commons is the elected lower house of the UK Parliament

indicators.note: bizarrely means in a strange way, so the following word appears in a strange order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: MPs are oddly regarded as sensible people.
explanation.walkthrough: The House of Commons is Britain's elected chamber of MPs.
explanation.definitionFit: A common-sense approach is practical and sensible, which is what rational describes.

clue.text: Particularly cool piano overturned in raid

indicators.note: in puts the overturned letters inside the raid word

parts.note: a sally is a sudden sortie or raid

indicators.note: overturned means turned upside down, so in a down entry these letters run the other way

parts.note: to ice something is to cool it
p is the musical marking for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A trendy piano is knocked over during a burglary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cool' suggests trendy, but it is the verb meaning to chill; a sally is a sortie by besieged troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Specially and particularly both mean especially, for a specific purpose or to an unusual degree.

clue.text: Curses business charges?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: denounces or detests, a verb
second meaning, read cryptically as two words: the fees of a business executive

explanation.walkthrough: Split as EXEC RATES, the word becomes the rates an executive charges; the question mark flags that pun.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate is to denounce or call down evil upon, so execrates means damns or curses.

clue.text: Flash article containing so outsize layer of precious metal

indicators.note: containing means the article word holds the following two pieces inside it

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a flash
the is the definite article
ergo is Latin for therefore, so
OS is the clothing label for outsize

explanation.surface: A flashy story about a huge sheet of gold leaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Layer' means one that lays, not a coating: Mother Goose tales include the goose that laid golden eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: In the nursery tale linked to Mother Goose, a goose lays golden eggs, making her a producer of gold.

clue.text: Cast regularly seen inside at that place

definitions.text: Cast regularly seen inside at that place

indicators.note: inside places the kept letters within the place word

parts.note: there means at that place

indicators.note: regularly keeps every second letter of the preceding word

parts.note: the second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: A cast of actors keeps turning up in one particular spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a theatre is the place where a cast is regularly seen.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre is the building where actors perform, so it is where a company of players appears night after night.

clue.text: Stick for player in overheard row

indicators.note: overheard means caught by ear, so only the pronunciation of the row word matters

parts.note: a queue is a line of people, a row

explanation.surface: A musician's stick is mentioned in an argument someone eavesdropped on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a quarrel, but here it is a line of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A cue is the long tapered rod a snooker or billiards player strikes the ball with.

clue.text: One providing fare in time before boarding transport

indicators.note: a passenger boarding a vehicle gets inside it, so these letters go inside the transport word

parts.note: a car is a means of transport
T is the abbreviation for time
ere is a poetic word for before

explanation.surface: A bus driver collects fares on time before passengers get on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fare' suggests a ticket price, but it means food.
explanation.definitionFit: A caterer supplies food and drink for events, and fare is an old word for food.

clue.text: Winged creature following grouse

parts.note: a bee is a flying insect
f. is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: A flying insect is chasing a game bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grouse' wants to be the bird, but it is the verb or noun for a complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: A beef and a grouse are both slang for a complaint or grievance.

clue.text: Pound raised is small joy

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means lifted from bottom to top, reading backwards

parts.note: lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight
taken as written
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A small price rise brings little happiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Bliss is perfect happiness, a state of great joy.

clue.text: Overseer of US agency involved in attack with soldiers

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped up within, so the agency sits inside the attack word

parts.note: a fit is a sudden attack, as of coughing
the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A supervisor at an American spy agency is caught up in a military raid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' looks like part of the definition but supplies its own letters. Other ranks are soldiers who are not officers.
explanation.definitionFit: An officiator presides over or conducts proceedings, so is the person overseeing them.

clue.text: Scavenger beginning to rip neat clothes

indicators.note: to clothe something is to cover it all round, so the cattle word wraps the letter

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle; a cow is one

indicators.note: beginning to means only the start of the following word is taken

parts.note: the first letter of rip

explanation.surface: A scavenger starts tearing apart someone's tidy clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' looks like the adjective tidy, but it is the archaic noun for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: Crows feed on carrion and scraps, so they are classic scavenging birds.

clue.text: Domestic military information to protect Royal Navy area

indicators.note: to protect something is to surround it, so the information word goes around the pieces after it

parts.note: intel is short for intelligence
RN is the abbreviation for the Royal Navy
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Home intelligence services guard a naval zone.
explanation.definitionFit: Internal and domestic both describe affairs inside a country rather than foreign ones.

clue.text: Red mark on page crossing line

indicators.note: the mark word lies across the letter, so it is placed inside

parts.note: a caret is the proofreader's mark showing where to insert text
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A red pen mark on a page cuts across a line of text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red' suggests the ink colour, but it is the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is the British name for red Bordeaux wine, and also a deep purplish red colour.

clue.text: Pronounced flat grassland with sage in distinct phases

indicators.note: pronounced means spoken aloud, so only the sound of the grassland word counts

parts.note: the steppe is the flat grassy plain of Eurasia
sage as an adjective means wise

explanation.surface: A herb such as sage is planted on distinctly flat grassland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pronounced' looks like the adjective meaning marked, but it means spoken. 'Sage' wants to be the herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Stepwise describes progress made one step at a time, through separate stages.

clue.text: Scrumpy might be produced by this country farm, far away

indicators.note: the drink might be produced by rearranging, so its letters are a reworking of the answer plus one more
far away tells you to take the letters of far out of the word before it

parts.note: scrumpy is rough farmhouse cider from the West Country of England
taken as written

explanation.surface: Rough cider might be made by this nation's farms, a long way off.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs backwards: the answer plus M (farm without far) can be rearranged to make SCRUMPY.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyprus is an island country in the eastern Mediterranean.
